paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: This figure compares the error rate (one average minus test accuracy), computation cost, and GPU memory across our approach and baselines, for fine-tuning Llama-3-8B on ten NLP tasks with QAdapter.
model_annotation: The figure is a single-series vertical bar chart titled "QAdapter" that illustrates the computational cost in floating-point operations for several fine-tuning approaches, with one bar per method. The category axis is the horizontal x-axis, showing the method names in left-to-right order: "Full FT", "TAG", "Adapter", "MTLo-FT", "Q-Adapter", and "Ours"; the labels are rotated diagonally. The value axis is the vertical y-axis labeled "# FLOPs" and uses a logarithmic scale with major tick marks labeled at approximately 10^18, 10^19, and 10^20. There are six bars total: five baseline methods are shown as orange bars and the final method "Ours" is shown as a green bar. By visual estimation on the log scale, "Full FT" is around 6×10^19 FLOPs, "TAG" is around 2×10^19, "Adapter" is around 1.6–1.8×10^19, "MTLo-FT" is around 3–4×10^18, "Q-Adapter" is around 1.8–2×10^18, and "Ours" (green) is around 2×10^18. The bars are not stacked or grouped, there is no legend, and no individual bars appear annotated beyond their color difference (orange versus green).
